newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee market remains dull.
newsitem.headline: German coffee market remains dull.

text.p: Green coffee markets in Germany have been untroubled by last week's report of a 20 percent chance of frost in Brazilian growing regions, traders said on Monday.
Cash buyers brushed aside a report from forecasters Cropcast which said cold weather could reach Brazil's coffee belt by the middle of this week.
They cited other weather reports saying high pressure expected to build in Argentina was likely to pass well to the south of the coffee areas.

"The chance of weather problems in Brazil may give underlying support to New York arabica futures, but this is not echoed in the physical market, where buyers are happy to remain sidelined," one trader said.
"Sellers and buyers have not yet agreed on new crop prices," he added.
Traders said industry stocks were comfortable and demand for roasted coffee from wholesalers was limited because of a seasonal lull in coffee-drinking amid hot summer temperatures.
Central American shippers appeared in no hurry to market the new crop, with fresh negotiations not expected before the end of August.

Arabica buyers of Central American origins were holding out for price reductions once markets move out of the Brazilian winter period but they were taking some African and Asian material, importers said.
They also reported some Colombian sales for Oct/Dec.
There was also some sizeable robusta business, including Vientamese new crop.
This kept Ivorian robusta G-2 steady on the week at $78 cif per 50 kg.
Second hand Brazils for Sept shipment remained at $166 fob and Colombia excelso for the same month rose $3 to $193.
